Is gender reassignment surgery covered by insurance? Insurance application conditions and points to note

2024 11/01
PR available
orchidectomy
October 30, 2024November 1, 2024

“Is gender reassignment surgery covered by insurance?”

“Is it possible to change the family register after gender reassignment surgery?”

Gender reassignment surgery is an operation for people who suffer from gender identity disorder.Medical insurance became applicable in Japan in 2018.

If you apply, you can change your family register and become the gender you desire, both physically and in your family register.

However, there are multiple conditions for insurance to apply, and as of 2024, these conditions have become extremely strict.

If you are currently receiving treatment for gender identity disorder,Depending on the treatment, it may not be covered by insurance.

Here we will explain the methods and sites related to gender reassignment, including insurance coverage conditions and costs for gender reassignment surgery, and how to apply for a change in family register.

What you can learn from this article
  • Basic knowledge of gender reassignment surgery
  • Conditions for insurance coverage for gender reassignment surgery
  • Countermeasures for surgical expenses when insurance does not apply
Table of contents

What is gender reassignment surgery? Introducing the details of surgery and surgeries that are/are not covered by insurance

Gender reassignment surgery, also known as sex reassignment surgery, is an operation to match a person's physical and mental gender.

This is a surgery for people who are suffering from gender identity disorder, MtF, or FtM, and the difference between what is covered by insurance and what is not is as follows.

  • What is covered by insurance: Treatments for gender identity disorder such as mastectomy and orchidectomy
  • Items not covered by insurance: Cosmetic items such as facial surgery, hair removal, and breast augmentation

Here, we will explain the basics of gender reassignment surgery, including its contents and insurance coverage conditions.

Is it possible to change gender after gender reassignment surgery?申請についての紹介

If you undergo gender reassignment surgery in the treatment of gender identity disorder, if the conditions are met.Gender on family register can also be changedIt is.

In this case, the notification must be submitted to the family court rather than to the town hall.

If you want to change your gender on your family register, you can change it if the following conditions apply:

  1. Being diagnosed with gender identity disorder by two or more doctors
  2. Be over 18 years old
  3. Not currently married
  4. No current minor children
  5. Having an appearance that approximates the genital parts of the other gender

Source:Changes in the treatment of gender | Courts

*Until 2020, the condition included "having no gonads or permanently lacking gonadal function," but this has now become invalid.

In addition, prepare a petition, a copy of your family register, and the 800 yen revenue stamp fee, and apply to the court that has jurisdiction over your residence.

Details about the application documents and other documents required for application can be found on the court's website.

About insurance coverage

Gender reassignment surgery became covered by insurance in Japan in 2018.

Therefore, it is possible to undergo gender reassignment surgery for about 30% of the medical cost.

However, insurance for gender reassignment surgery is still in its infancy, and there are various conditions for coverage.

Here, we will explain the cases in which gender reassignment surgery is covered by insurance and the cases in which it is not.

Differences between what is covered by insurance and what is not for gender reassignment surgery

The following is a breakdown of gender reassignment surgeries that are covered by insurance and those that are not.

What is covered by insurance?
  • mastectomy surgery
  • urethroplasty surgery
  • phalloplasty surgery
  • Penis/orchidectomy surgery
  • perineoplasty surgery
  • Vaginostomy
  • hysterectomy surgery

etc.

What is not covered by insurance?
  • hair removal
  • Breast augmentation
  • plastic surgery
  • hormone injection

As mentioned above, the cases where gender reassignment surgery is covered by insurance are:Surgery such as removing parts and organs that have gender-specific characteristics or transplanting substitutesIt is.

Breast augmentation surgery, hair removal, facial cosmetic surgery, hormone injections, etc. are not covered by insurance and must be treated at your own expense.

Conditions for insurance coverage for gender reassignment surgery

Insurance coverage for gender reassignment surgery is not limited to the details of the surgery.

Gender reassignment surgery is only covered by insurance if it is performed at a hospital that is accredited by the government and certified by the GID Society.

As of October 2024, the clinics certified by the GID Society are as follows.

  • Okayama University Hospital
  • Social Medical Corporation Kosei Hospital
  • University of Yamanashi School of Medicine Hospital
  • Nagoya University Hospital
  • Sapporo Medical University Hospital
  • Okinawa Prefectural Chubu Hospital
  • Medical Corporation Meirikai Gyotoku General Hospital
  • Sapporo Central Hospital

These hospitals are licensed by the government and accredited by the GID Society, so they are covered by insurance.

Surgery fees vary by hospital, so please check with the clinic.

We will introduce the average cost of some surgeries as self-pay medical expenses.

Mastectomy surgery: 700,000 yen

Hysterectomy: 800,000 yen

Penile plastic surgery: 2 million yen

Vaginoplasty surgery: 1.5 million yen

If covered by insurance, 30% of these surgical costs will be covered.

For example, a mastectomy costs 30% of 700,000 yen, so the surgery can be done for 210,000 yen.

保険適用の注意点！ Insurance does not cover treatment if you are receiving hormone therapy.

As mentioned above, gender reassignment surgery is covered by insurance at certain hospitals, but there are only a limited number of cases in which it is actually covered.

One of the reasons for this is treatment with hormone injections.

When performing surgery that is covered by insurance, if the treatment is self-pay, it will not be covered by insurance.

This is the so-called"Mixed treatment"In the case of mixed medical treatment, insurance may also apply.All of this is considered self-pay medical treatment.

Why are all mixed medical treatments self-pay?

The Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare prohibits mixed medical treatment for the following reasons:

  • Medical treatments whose safety has not been confirmed will also be covered by insurance, leading to the promotion of treatments whose effectiveness and safety have not been established.
  • The burden on patients may unreasonably increase as they will also have to pay for expenses not covered by insurance.

Reference:Regarding the combined use of insured and non-insured treatment | Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare

Currently, hormone treatment is included in self-pay medical treatment, so if hormone treatment is performed before gender reassignment surgery, it will be treated as mixed treatment and will not be covered by insurance.

Currently, if you want insurance to cover gender reassignment surgery, you must undergo a mastectomy or other surgery that can be performed before hormone treatment.

What to do if insurance does not cover gender reassignment surgery

If you are having sex reassignment surgery, if there is no hospital nearby that will be covered by insurance, or if the treatment will be mixed as mentioned above, it will not be covered by insurance.

In that case, the medical expenses will be high, which will put a heavy burden on your daily life.

In that case, there are two possible countermeasures:

  • Take a medical loan
  • Apply for medical expense deduction on your final tax return

Here, we will introduce ways to deal with medical expenses when insurance does not cover them.

Use a loan to spread the financial burden

By utilizing medical expense loans,You can spread the financial burden.

You can also take advantage of loans from conventional banks and financial institutions, but medical expense loans can be used at lower interest rates.

However, because there is an examination, it is not always possible to receive a loan.

When using a medical loan, you can broadly divide it into two: bank-based medical loans and credit-based medical loans.

Although there are slight differences depending on the financial institution, the general differences between bank medical loans and credit sales medical loans are as follows.

Bank-based medical loans are subject to strict screening such as credit information and income, so if you are not approved, use a credit-based medical loan.

Also, when taking out a loan, it is important to have a solid repayment plan in advance.

Apply for medical expense deduction on your final tax return

By filing a final tax return, you can deduct medical expenses.

Medical expense deduction is a tax deduction system that you can receive if your annual medical expenses exceed a certain amount.

If the cost of gender reassignment surgery is expensive, you can reduce your tax burden by taking advantage of medical expense deductions.

By keeping the receipts you need when filing your tax return and taking advantage of deductions, you may be able to get some of your expenses back.

If your annual medical expenses exceed 100,000 yen, you can receive a medical expense deduction on your final tax return.

The amount of medical expense deduction is calculated using the following formula.

(Total amount of medical expenses actually paid - (1) amount) - (2) amount (up to 2 million yen)

(1) Amount to be compensated by insurance money, etc.

(2) 100,000 yen

Quote:No.1120 When paying medical expenses (medical expense deduction) | National Tax Agency 

In recent years, it has become easier to file a tax return because it is now possible to file a tax return online, and there are also extensive procedural manuals.

It may take some time, but it may lead to significant savings, so don't forget to do it.

Summary

This article introduced the basic knowledge of gender reassignment surgery and the conditions under which it is covered by insurance.

The insurance system for gender reassignment surgery is still in its infancy, and the conditions for coverage have not yet been fully established.

There are high hurdles for insurance coverage, such as the small number of hospitals that cover it and the fact that insurance won't cover any hormone treatments that are nearly essential for FtM or MtF.

However, there is a good chance that this will be eased in the future, and even now it is easy to find ways to reduce the monthly burden, such as medical loans and medical expense deductions.

However, gender reassignment surgery is an expensive but time-consuming procedure, and you may lose your resolve during the procedure.

If you really want to start using it for the first time or not, consult your doctor and weigh the pros and cons before doing so.
